title: Bab al-Mandab Burning: Yemen's war reaches the strait
oneLine: The Houthis have pushed down Yemen's coast to the mouth of the Red Sea, Saudi Arabia is fighting back, and its Emirati ally has become a rival.

whoIsWho.stance: Wants the Houthis off the coast or a deal that stops the strikes on Saudi cities.
Holds Sanaa and Mokha; wants Saudi-paid salaries and recognition as Yemen's power.
Backs southern forces and ports in Yemen; at odds with Riyadh over Yemen and Sudan.
Yemen's recognised government in Aden, Saudi-backed, outgunned on the coast.
Southern separatists who 'dissolved' in January but are still armed.

whyItMatters: Bab al-Mandab is the southern gate to the Suez Canal. Houthi attacks have already sent ships around Africa, emptying Egypt's canal. A Saudi-Emirati split would leave the region's richest powers fighting each other's proxies.

timeline.text: The Houthis seize Yemen's capital, Sanaa.
A Saudi-led coalition goes to war against them.
The Houthis start attacking ships in the Red Sea over Gaza.
The UAE-backed STC says it will dissolve after its leader flees to Abu Dhabi.
The Houthis take Mokha; reports say Perim too.
A Houthi missile kills 13 at Riyadh's airport.
Government forces pull back from the strait to defend Aden.
